newsitem.title: FRANCE: French minister sticks to anti-Clinton charge.
newsitem.headline: French minister sticks to anti-Clinton charge.

text.p: A French cabinet minister refused on Wednesday to withdraw a statement that an African tour by U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher was aimed at promoting President Bill Clinton's re-election.
"I'm not retracting what I said. Nowhere have I said anything which was not true," junior cooperation minister Jacques Godfrain told reporters.

Godfrain was responding to a demand by the State Department in Washington that he withdraw what spokesman Nicholas Burns called "a ludicrous charge made by someone who's not paid attention to what the United States has done".

"I said that U.S. aid to Africa is declining and it is. I said President Cinton never went to Africa and he didn't. I said that Clinton never pronounced the word Africa at the United Nations and he never did," Godfrain said.
"I also said we are just days away from the American election," said Godfrain, adding an African folk saying that "the truth does not blind but sometimes it prevents from seeing."

Godfrain, who is in charge of French ties with the continent, sparked the row when he said last week he was "delighted to see (Clinton) showing interest in Africa and making it a priority three weeks before the presidential elections."
U.S. officials said the French were upset by Christopher's trip because they saw it as trespassing on a French domain.
Christopher, who returned on Monday from his five-nation tour, said in a speech in South Africa that "Africa needs the support of all its many friends, not the exclusive patronage of

French Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt said on Wednesday that Foreign Minister Herve de Charette respected Christopher as "his colleague and friend...and we ourselves have the highest appreciation for the international role of the United States".
"We consider this affair closed," Rummelhardt added.
